title: Government Policy
summary: --Government policy (May Subd Geog) is a free-floating topical subdivision used under topical headings and headings for classes of persons or ethnic groups, except where a phrase heading ([...] policy or [...] and state) already exists and except under headings for inherently governmental activities (City planning; Finance, Public; Crime prevention). Under places, specific policy subdivisions are used (--Economic policy, --Social policy, etc.); only --Economic policy and --Social policy may be subdivided chronologically.
validation_rules: `--Government policy` is a free-floating topical subdivision ($x), (May Subd Geog), used under topical headings and headings for classes of persons or ethnic groups, e.g. `Older people--Government policy--United States--Congresses`, `Adolescent parents--Government policy--United States--States`. (H 1642 Background, sec. 1)
Geographic subdivision follows `--Government policy` (i.e. `[topic]--Government policy--[place]`), since the subdivision itself is May Subd Geog. (H 1642 sec. 1 examples)

Do not use `--Government policy` under a heading for which a corresponding phrase heading of the form `[...] policy` (e.g. `Urban policy`, `Housing policy`) or `[...] and state` (e.g. `Education and state`, `Theater and state`) has been established; use the phrase heading. (H 1642 sec. 1, 2)

Do not use `--Government policy` under headings designating activities that are inherently governmental in nature, e.g. `City planning`; `Finance, Public`; `Crime prevention`. (H 1642 sec. 1 Exception)

Under names of places, use the specific free-floating policy subdivisions from H 1140, e.g. `--Cultural policy`, `--Commercial policy`, `--Economic policy`, `--Military policy`, `--Population policy`, `--Social policy`; the corresponding phrase headings are not authorized for geographic subdivision. (H 1642 sec. 3)
`--Economic policy` and `--Social policy` may be subdivided chronologically (each use is established), e.g. `[place]--Economic policy--[period]`. (H 1642 sec. 4)

Do not subdivide chronologically `--Government policy`, `--Commercial policy`, `--Cultural policy`, `--Military policy`, or `--Population policy`; assign additional headings to bring out a period. (H 1642 sec. 4)
New headings of the form `[...] policy` or `[...] and state` are not to be proposed; existing ones remain valid. (H 1642 sec. 2)

sections.heading: 1. Use of the free-floating subdivision.
sections.text:
Use the subdivision --Government policy (May Subd Geog) as described above under any heading for which a corresponding phrase heading has not already been established. Examples:

```
Title: Final report, the 1981 White House Conference on Aging.
650 #0 $a Older people $x Government policy $z United States $v Congresses.

Title: Overview of state policies related to adolescent parenthood.
650 #0 $a Adolescent parents $x Government policy $z United States $x States.
```

Exception: Do not use --Government policy under headings designating activities that are inherently governmental in nature, for example, City planning; Finance, Public; Crime prevention.

sections.heading: 2. Use of existing phrase headings.
sections.text: Continue to use existing headings that have been established in the form [ . . . ] policy or [ . . . ] and state. Do not, however, propose new headings of this type.

sections.heading: 3. Free-floating subdivisions for specific types of policy.
sections.text: Some phrase headings for policy are not authorized for geographic subdivision because corresponding subdivisions are used under names of places, for example, --Cultural policy, --Commercial policy, --Economic policy, --Military policy, --Population policy, --Social policy. See H 1140 for the complete list of free-floating subdivisions used under names of places.

sections.heading: 4. Chronological subdivision.
sections.text:
The subdivisions --Economic policy and --Social policy may be subdivided chronologically. Establish each use of a chronological subdivision.

Do not chronologically subdivide --Government policy, --Commercial policy, --Cultural policy, --Military policy, or --Population policy. Assign additional headings to bring out a specific time period.
